content:
tim-sales: Heads-up — Fenix Health POC next Tue. They want Redwood Private in their AWS account, but they also want egress through their corporate proxy with a single static IP. They asked about PrivateLink vs a direct VPC peering approach and want a preflight checklist for their network/security teams.

alex.solutions: Thanks — can we confirm if they plan to host the Redwood nodes in their VPC (customer-managed) or have Redwood host and accept connections into their VPC via PrivateLink?

tim-sales: Customer-managed. They’ll host our private package inside their account but want control over outbound egress and firewall rules. Also asked whether we can preserve source IPs behind NAT.

raj-netops: Quick notes:
- VPC peering: simple L3 routing, full routing between VPCs but requires both sides to accept routes and doesn’t traverse IGW/NAT.
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints): provides service-level connectivity via ENIs in consumer subnets; good for not sharing full routing, works well across accounts but has per-ENI cross-AZ cost.
- If they want single static egress IP, they need a NAT gateway (EIP) or their corporate egress proxy. We don’t preserve original client IP behind NAT. If source-IP preservation is a hard req, they must use proxy that injects client info (e.g., X-Forwarded-For) or use a routing setup that avoids SNAT.

emily-security: From sec questionnaire POV:
- Required outbound: HTTPS to our control plane endpoints (TLS, port 443) and health/metrics to our metrics collector (usually 443 as well). We should provide explicit FQDNs not IPs.
- Management plane (can be PrivateLink): customer must allow inbound interface endpoints to our service NLB if using provider-hosted model — but since they host, they need outbound to our image repo and updates (ports 443), and access to S3 endpoints if using regional artifact storage.

tim-sales: They also asked about firewall rules for streaming responses — anything extra besides 443?

alex.solutions: For streaming (gRPC/websocket) typical setup is 443. If they run our runtime in their VPC and use internal load balancers for service-to-service, you'll see ephemeral ports for backend-to-backend health checks; we usually recommend these firewall rules (customer side):

```
# Allow outbound from Redwood instances to:
- tcp 443 to *.redwood-inference-controlplane.aws
- tcp 443 to registry.redwood-inference.aws (image pulls)
- tcp 53 to customer DNS resolver (if they use custom DNS)
# If using PrivateLink (our control plane as service):
- allow interface endpoint ENIs from service to consumer subnets
```

raj-netops: Add-on: If they use VPC peering, ensure no overlapping CIDRs; peering doesn't support transitive routing so any hub/spoke needs TGW. If they want cross-account private endpoints + central egress, TGW+route tables is the usual pattern.

emily-security: For questionnaire items we can fill in:
- Do we require customer network to open any inbound ports to internet? No — outbound TLS only for image pulls/control plane by default.
- Is mTLS supported between components? We support mutual auth for sensitive setups (note: requires config on their side)

tim-sales: Pricing question from customer: "Does using Private in our account change pricing vs Redwood-hosted? Any additional infra costs?"

alex.solutions: Short answer: yes — hosting in-customer shifts infra costs to customer (EC2/EKS/GPU instances, NAT gw, NLB/ENI charges). Redwood billing for Private is a platform/license fee + optional support. Dedicated/reserved capacity pricing is separate. I can send a ballpark doc but they'll need to budget for EIP/NAT gateway hours and per-ENI PrivateLink costs if used.

tim-sales: They also want a one-page network checklist for their netsec team.

alex.solutions: Draft checklist (can paste into their SQA):
1) Confirm VPC CIDR and ensure no overlap with Redwood control plane VPC (if peering).
2) Decide routing pattern: VPC Peering (L3) vs PrivateLink (service endpoints). Tradeoffs: peering = broader access, PrivateLink = scoped service-level access.
3) If single static egress IP required -> provision NAT Gateway + EIP or corporate forward proxy; note NAT adds cost.
4) Allow outbound TLS (443) to the set of FQDNs we’ll provide for image pulls and control plane; avoid IP-only allowlist if possible.
5) If using PrivateLink: allocate subnets for ENIs (one per AZ), and allow ENI SGs inbound/outbound as documented.
6) DNS: ensure they can resolve service endpoint names; if they use Route53 private zones, add records as needed.
7) Audit & logging: enable VPC Flow Logs to S3/CloudWatch and share retention requirements.

emily-security: I'll populate the security questionnaire fields for networking and send a redacted copy.

deply-bot: (deploy-bot) link: https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/private-deploy-networking

tim-sales: Perfect. Alex/Emily — can you join customer call Monday 10am PT? Want to run through checklist and pricing. Customer stressed timeline: POC by Tue.

alex.solutions: I’m in.

emily-security: I can make it for first 30 mins then drop.

raj-netops: I’ll join for network handoff.

tim-sales: Great — I’ll send calendar invite and attach the checklist + minimal firewall snippet. Thanks all :thumbsup:
